themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Collapse
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 80 THIS WEEK versus a 9.8 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 720% increase (z-score: 10.15)—suggesting rapid deterioration of roads in East Harlem that aligns with repeated DOT budget requests for street repairs and may signal a localized pavement crisis demanding immediate investigation.
evidence: 80 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 9.8 weekly average (prior 8 weeks)
Convergence: Street repairs appear in CB budget requests as recurring unfunded need
reporting_angles: Ground-truth: photo-document worst affected blocks and interview residents about potholes/flooding impacts
Accountability: Why did DOT's street repair requests go unfunded year after year, and what triggered this week's surge?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints hit 4 THIS WEEK versus 0.1 weekly average—a 3100% spike with z-score 11.72 (the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset)—suggesting either coordinated tree removal, construction-related damage, or a reporting artifact that requires urgent field verification given East Harlem's limited canopy.
evidence: 4 illegal tree damage complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average (prior 8 weeks)
3100% spike with z-score 11.72 (highest severity in dataset)
Convergence with damaged tree complaints up 700% last week (3 vs 0.4 avg), suggesting broader tree stress
reporting_angles: Spatial mapping: Identify which blocks or developments are epicenter of tree damage complaints
Investigation: Is this tied to 58-62 E. 125th St. rezoning or other active construction permits (454 filed in 90 days)?

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Crisis This Week
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints jumped to 7 THIS WEEK from 1.5 weekly average—a 367% spike (z-score: 5.5)—marking the newest environmental signal and suggesting acute air pollution, construction dust, or odor complaints that warrant source investigation and resident interviews.
evidence: 7 air quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average (prior 8 weeks)
Convergence with street condition spike (80 complaints this week) and tree damage—suggests possible construction-related dust/debris emissions
reporting_angles: Source identification: Interview residents about smell/visibility changes; cross-reference with active DOB permits
Health angle: Are asthma-related ED visits up? Contact DOHMH for respiratory complaint data

themes_detail.label: Street Light Failures Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints spiked to 16 LAST WEEK from 3.4 weekly average—a 374% increase (z-score: 6.53)—and street lights appear as a repeated unfunded CB budget request, indicating chronic underfunding of DOT maintenance that is now visibly failing and creating safety/crime concerns.
evidence: 16 street light complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.4 weekly average (prior 8 weeks)
Repeated CB budget request: 'Repair or provide new street lights (DOT)' signals multi-year unfunded need
reporting_angles: Safety narrative: Interview residents/merchants about crime, pedestrian safety, and lighting outages after dark
Budget accountability: Why has DOT street light funding request been denied year after year?

themes_detail.label: Residential Disposal Crisis Last Week
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints surged to 8 LAST WEEK from 0.5 weekly average—a 1500% spike (z-score: 8.66)—and graffiti/cleaning appears in CB recurring budget requests, suggesting possible sanitation worker shortage, garbage collection failure, or illegal dumping requiring urgent verification.
evidence: 8 residential disposal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (prior 8 weeks)
Convergence: CB requests 'Increase Graffiti Removal/Cleaning (DSNY)' annually—suggests chronic sanitation underresourcing
reporting_angles: Ground truth: Document accumulation on streets; interview residents about pickup schedules
DSNY accountability: Was there a collection disruption last week? Labor/vehicle shortage?
